review_candidates.title: Senior Network Engineer, Energy Storage
review_candidates.description: About Redwood Materials Redwood Materials was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, co-founder and former CTO of Tesla, on a simple but radical idea: the critical minerals powering the energy transition already exist. They just need to come back. Today Redwood is the largest lithium-ion battery recycler in North America — recovering, refining, and redeploying critical minerals from end-of-life batteries back into the supply chain. On the energy side, Redwood has deployed the largest second-life battery project in the world, delivering power to AI data centers in months rather than years using proprietary energy architecture engineered entirely in-house. The company is profitable, the market it operates in is projected to grow 20 to 50 times over the next decade, and Redwood is the only company with the supply chain, the technology, and the operational scale to lead it. Position Summary: The Senior Network Engineer, Energy Storage leads network design and deployment for the Energy organization’s battery energy storage system (BESS) and microgrid projects. The role independently designs, builds, commissions, and supports industrial networks at company and customer energy sites, working directly with Energy engineers, site operations, and contractors. This is a fully on-site role at BMC 1. Designs are reviewed at critical points by the network engineer team. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Designs standardized, resilient networks for BESS and microgrid sites to internal or customer specifications, including core and field switching, routing, redundancy, NAT, and repeatable per-site configurations so spare hardware fits any site Leads network builds, commissioning, cutovers, and customer handovers, coordinating schedules and outage windows with Energy engineering, site operations, and contractors Troubleshoots network faults that interact with power systems, such as DC power and isolation requirements for field switches, voltage drop on long cable runs, UPS and automatic transfer switch behavior, and inverter and controller communications Specifies and qualifies industrial network hardware, optics, power supplies, and cabling, including lab testing of designs and Energy’s custom proprietary hardware before deployment Implements monitoring of network, UPS, and transfer switch equipment, correlates network logs with inverter and site controller data, and develops segmentation and secure remote access that keep energy site networks separate from campus IT and OT networks Keeps stakeholders informed on designs, schedules, and findings, and maintains as-built documentation, network diagrams, configurations, and runbooks for each energy site Supports Information Technology network needs outside of Energy as assigned, based on Energy workload Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience 5+ years of enterprise or industrial network engineering experience, including design and deployment of routed and switched networks, plus experience in BESS, solar, microgrid, substation, or SCADA environments and with industrial protocols such as Modbus and CAN bus; CCNP, JNCIP, or equivalent certification preferred Working knowledge of routing and switching (OSPF, BGP, VLANs, link aggregation, spanning tree), redundancy designs, firewalls, VPN, and network segmentation, with a knack for keeping designs simple and standardized for consistent support across sites Solid grasp of electrical power fundamentals, including AC and DC power, grounding, UPS and transfer switch operation, and how inverters and battery systems connect to the grid; comfortable reading electrical one-line diagrams, wiring diagrams, and equipment specifications Comfortable working around high-voltage equipment, primarily de-energized and occasionally energized, using required PPE and following site electrical safety procedures Clear communicator who can explain technical concepts to audiences with varying technical knowledge, including non-IT employees and customers Willing to travel up to 50% of the time to remote sites and to work outside standard hours, including evenings and weekends, for cutovers, site outages, and maintenance windows The position is full-time. Compensation will be commensurate with experience.
